newsitem.title: UK: S&P affirms Swiss Bank, units ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms Swiss Bank, units ratings.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it affirmed its long- and short-term ratings of Swiss Bank Corp and its units.
It said in a statement that the rating outlook was stable.

S&P said it affirmed SBC's senior debt rating at AA plus, subordinated debt at AA, commercial paper at A1 minus, certificates of deposit at AA plus/ A1 plus and counterparty ratings at AA plus/A1 plus.
"The rating action follows today's announcement that the bank (SBC) will record a substantial loss in 1996 following various extraordinary charges," S&P said

Although SBC will report a loss in 1966, S&P said it viewed this largely as an accounting issue. It said SBC's specific provisions for problem credits were already believed to be adequate and the risk profile of the group remained unchanged.
It said the bank's new provisioning policy amounted to the lowering of one reserve (retained earnings) to allow creation of another (the Actuarial Credit Risk Accounting reserve ACRA).

S&P said the volatility of the group's profit and loss account would be dampened as the annual credit charge would be reduced or increased (by using the ACRA resrve) to reflect the group's long-term historical loan loss experience, estimated by SBC to be between 550 and 600 million Swiss francs.
"However, the group's overall capital position will still rise and fall, via the ACRA reserve, according to asset quality trends," it said.
S&P said the ratings of the following units were affirmed.
Swiss Bank Corp (Overseas Ltd) -- senior debt
SBC Warburg Australia Ltd -- senior debt
-- counterparty
-- commercial paper
SBC Warburg Australia Holdings -- commercial paper
SBC (Sydney) -- commercial paper
Swiss Bank Corp (Jersey) -- senior debt
-- subordinated debt
SBC Finance (Cayman Islands) -- senior debt
SBC Finance (DE) Inc -- commercial paper
-- International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 8682
